name: openrouteservice (hosted API)
provider: HeiGIT gGmbH (Heidelberg Institute for Geoinformation Technology)
free_limits: Standard plan (0 EUR, 'Free to use for everyone'), daily / per-minute: Directions V2 2,000 / 40; Matrix V2 500 / 40; Optimization (VROOM) 500 / 40; Isochrones V2 500 / 20; Geocoding 3,000 / 100; Snap V2 2,000 / 100; POIs 500 / 60; Elevation 2,000 / 40; Export V2 100 / 5. Per-request caps: Directions 50 waypoints, 6,000 km; Matrix 3,500 origin x destination cells (e.g. 50 x 50); Optimization 3 vehicles and 50 routes; Isochrones 5 locations. Collaborative plan (5x the quotas) is only for humanitarian, academic, governmental or not-for-profit organisations. On-premise install: no limits.
commercial_use: Allowed - not restricted. The plan page says 'Free to use for everyone' and the Terms of Service contain a 'Use by an Entity' clause for companies and no non-commercial clause. Conditions: one account per person for all HeiGIT APIs; the ToS lists 'Transmit personal data' as prohibited conduct; a private company is NOT eligible for the larger Collaborative plan.
auth_required: API key (free HeiGIT account)
attribution_or_license_terms: Attribution required: '(c) openrouteservice by HeiGIT | Data from OpenStreetMap'. Results obtained from openrouteservice are licensed CC-BY-SA 4.0; underlying data is OpenStreetMap (ODbL). Optimization: 'Developed by vroom | Hosted by HeiGIT | Routing by openrouteservice | Data from OpenStreetMap'.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Plans page and Terms of Service read in a browser on account.heigit.org (openrouteservice.org/plans and /terms-of-service now redirect there). Per-request restrictions read from the official docs. Surprises: the optimization endpoint is capped at 3 vehicles per request on the hosted API; results carry CC-BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike), not just attribution; the ToS forbids transmitting personal data; the terms say HeiGIT advises against using it as the sole source for critical routing. No SLA. The API host is moving to api.heigit.org according to third-party notes - not confirmed on an official page.

name: LocationIQ (geocoding, maps, routing)
free_limits: Free plan: 5,000 requests/day, 2 requests/second, 60 requests/minute.
commercial_use: Restricted ('Limited Commercial Use'): the free plan may be used in commercial projects only if a prominent link back to LocationIQ is shown in the website or app.
auth_required: API key (account)
attribution_or_license_terms: Link-back required on the free plan, format given on the pricing page: Search by LocationIQ.com. Data is OpenStreetMap-based, so OSM attribution applies as well. Caching: free accounts may cache request-response pairs for up to 48 hours only; server-side caching of map tiles is not allowed.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Pricing page and its FAQ read. Surprise: results may be cached for 48 hours only on the free plan (paid customers may keep them while they remain customers), so geocodes cannot be stored permanently on the free tier; commercial use is conditional on the visible link-back.

name: OpenFreeMap public vector tiles
free_limits: Public instance is free with no registration, no API key, no cookies, and 'no limits on the number of map views or requests'. Only bulk/offline downloads are limited: at most 3,000 tiles or 50 MB per download, max 4 parallel requests, unique User-Agent.
commercial_use: Allowed - the site answers 'Yes' to commercial use.
auth_required: none
attribution_or_license_terms: Attribution is required (OpenFreeMap / OpenMapTiles / OpenStreetMap contributors); MapLibre adds it automatically. Data is OpenStreetMap (ODbL).
verification_note: Home page read. Confirmed free, keyless, commercial use allowed, attribution required. The site states no SLA guarantees and no personalised support are offered; it is donation-funded and can be self-hosted. Risk is availability only, not cost.

name: Nominatim public server (nominatim.openstreetmap.org)
free_limits: No heavy use: absolute maximum of 1 request per second per application (all its users together). Valid HTTP Referer or identifying User-Agent required. Results must be cached on your side. Bulk geocoding: single thread, one machine, and scripts that run longer than a day or at regular intervals are restricted to 4 requests per minute. Auto-complete, systematic queries, scraping and reselling results are unacceptable uses.
commercial_use: Restricted - not forbidden, but the policy warns commercial applications that it is a donated service with no guarantee and that the policy may change without notice; a service whose primary function is geocoding must run its own instance.
auth_required: none (identifying User-Agent or Referer mandatory)
attribution_or_license_terms: ODbL - OpenStreetMap attribution must be clearly displayed.
verification_note: Usage policy read. Suitable only for occasional, user-triggered lookups (one address at a time) with caching; NOT suitable for geocoding a customer master in bulk, for type-ahead search, or as a dependency with an uptime expectation. The 1 request/second limit is per application, not per user, so 230 users share it. Self-hosting Nominatim is the route for anything heavier.

name: Overpass API public instance (overpass-api.de) and OpenStreetMap data licence
provider: FOSSGIS e.V. / Roland Olbricht (Overpass); OpenStreetMap Foundation (data)
free_limits: Guideline for the public instance: a maximum of about 10,000 requests per day and download volume below about 1 GB per day per user. Heavier users are expected to run their own instance; load shedding starts with heavy users first. For whole-region extracts use a planet dump instead of stitched queries.
commercial_use: Allowed - the usage guideline does not restrict commercial use and ODbL permits it, subject to the licence obligations.
auth_required: none
attribution_or_license_terms: ODbL 1.0. Must credit OpenStreetMap and make clear the data is available under the Open Database License. Share-alike: 'If you alter or build upon our data, you may distribute the result only under the same license.'
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Overpass usage guidance and the OSM copyright page read. The share-alike duty is triggered by DISTRIBUTING an adapted database; whether a purely internal database of pharmacies enriched from OSM triggers it was not confirmed from the pages opened (the ODbL legal text and the OSMF community guidelines were not read) - treat as a point to check before merging OSM data into the customer master. No SLA on the public instance.

name: geoBoundaries (gbOpen) and OCHA HDX 'Egypt - Subnational Administrative Boundaries'
provider: William & Mary geoLab (geoBoundaries); UN OCHA FISS on HDX, source CAPMAS (COD-AB)
free_limits: Free downloads, no quota stated. gbOpen Egypt: ADM0 (1 unit, 2017), ADM1 (27 governorates, 2017), ADM2 (365 units, 2020). No ADM3 in gbOpen. HDX COD-AB Egypt: boundaries down to Admin 3 (towns, districts, neighbourhoods), files as GDB, SHP, GeoJSON and XLSX, dataset last modified 26 January 2026, reference period 2017-04-21 to 2024-12-19.
commercial_use: Allowed with attribution. The geoBoundaries site says its CC BY 4.0 terms allow 'most commercial, noncommercial, and academic uses'; CC BY-IGO (HDX) also permits commercial use with attribution.
auth_required: none
attribution_or_license_terms: Mixed, per layer - NOT uniformly CC-BY: gbOpen Egypt ADM0 and ADM1 are Open Data Commons Open Database License 1.0 (source OpenStreetMap / Wambacher) and therefore carry ODbL attribution and share-alike; gbOpen Egypt ADM2 is CC BY 3.0 IGO (source OCHA ROMENA/HDX, CAPMAS). HDX COD-AB Egypt is 'Creative Commons Attribution for Intergovernmental Organisations (CC BY-IGO)', source Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS). geoBoundaries also asks for a visible credit with a link to www.geoboundaries.org.
verification_note: geoBoundaries API metadata for Egypt and the HDX dataset metadata (CKAN API) read; the HDX dataset web page itself would not render, so the licence comes from its API record. Surprise: Egypt's governorate layer (ADM1) in gbOpen is ODbL from OpenStreetMap dated 2017, not CC-BY; the cleanest single-licence source for governorate, district and sub-district is the HDX COD-AB set (CC BY-IGO). HDX caveats: 19 Admin-2 units along the Nile have duplicate English names inside one governorate (Arabic names are unique), 23 English names map to several Arabic names, and 14 'Zemam Out' Admin-2 units are absent from Admin 3 - join on codes, not names.

name: Mapillary API v4
free_limits: No price list exists. Rate limits per app: entity API 60,000 requests/minute; search API 10,000 requests/minute; vector tiles 50,000 requests/day.
commercial_use: Restricted - Terms section 12 permits commercial use only for (a) improving or developing products, services and datasets and (b) providing services to your clients; no use for real-time navigation or route guidance; an app must materially supplement Mapillary, not merely redistribute its content; safeguards against re-identifying or un-blurring imagery are required.
auth_required: API key (client access token from a registered application; OAuth 2.0 for user tokens)
attribution_or_license_terms: User imagery is under CC BY-SA unless Mapillary indicates otherwise (some data may be CC BY-NC-SA). Attribution: visibly display the Mapillary logo and link to the Mapillary home page or the image page, for images and for data derived from them.
verification_note: API documentation and Terms of Use read. The pages never use the word 'free', but there is no paid plan or price anywhere and the token comes from plain app registration; the help-centre licence article could not be reached (DNS failure). Coverage in Egypt was not checked. Share-alike applies to anything built from the images.

name: AlAdhan API (Hijri calendar conversion, Islamic special days, prayer times)
free_limits: Free, no account. No rate limit is stated on the official pages opened. An Islamic Network community-forum post (seen only as a search excerpt - the forum page would not load) gives about 12 requests/second per IP and a cumulative 70 requests per 7 seconds.
commercial_use: Not addressed - the terms page neither permits nor restricts commercial use.
auth_required: none
attribution_or_license_terms: None stated for API users (the site credits PrayTimes.org and shows '(c) Islamic Network and respective contributors').
verification_note: Terms page confirms: 'AlAdhan.com and the AlAdhan API are free and work without an account.' A live read of api.aladhan.com/v1/specialDays returned HTTP 200 with 78 entries and no key. NOT confirmed: the rate limit (official page not readable) and any commercial-use wording. Caution for payroll and leave: the special-days list is a fixed Hijri month/day table mixing public feasts with dozens of religious anniversaries, and a calculated Hijri date can differ by a day from Egypt's officially announced holiday - it cannot be the authority for Egyptian public holidays. No SLA.

name: Nager.Date / Nager.Holidays public holiday API
free_limits: Public API: no key, 'No Rate Limits', CORS enabled. Egypt (EG) is in the supported list (Africa coverage 92%). BUT the Terms of Service allow the Web API for 'private or non-profit projects' only.
commercial_use: Prohibited without payment - 'For commercial purposes we require active sponsorship.' GitHub Sponsors tiers: Commercial Starter 10 USD/month (commercial use + .NET library licence), Commercial Basic 20 USD/month (adds Docker container rights), Silver 50 USD/month, Gold 1,000 USD/month.
auth_required: none for the public API; a licence key for the Docker container and the NuGet package
attribution_or_license_terms: Repository licence is MIT, but the Docker image and the NuGet package both require a LICENSE_KEY obtained through sponsorship. Terms also forbid using the data to run your own holiday portal. No warranty of availability or accuracy.
verification_note: API page, country coverage page, Terms of Service, the GitHub README and the GitHub Sponsors page read. Surprise: the common belief 'free and self-hostable' is wrong for a company - commercial use needs an active paid sponsorship, and self-hosting (Docker) needs a licence key from the 20 USD/month tier. Also note Egypt's holidays are largely Hijri-based and officially announced, so any static dataset can be off by a day.

name: Cal.com (hosted) and Cal.diy (self-hosted community edition)
free_limits: Hosted Free plan: 0 USD 'free forever', 1 user, unlimited links (event types) and calendars, email and SMS notifications, 100+ app integrations, Stripe/PayPal payments. Teams 12 USD per user/month; Organizations 28 USD per user/month; Enterprise custom. Self-host: Cal.diy, no hosted version.
commercial_use: Hosted: allowed - the Terms license use 'for your internal business or personal purposes'; free plans carry no warranty and may be changed or ended with reasonable notice; resale/white-labelling prohibited. Self-host (Cal.diy): MIT permits commercial use, but the README says it 'is strictly recommended for personal, non-production use' and points commercial users to Cal.com.
auth_required: account (hosted); none for self-host beyond your own deployment
attribution_or_license_terms: Cal.com's production code is CLOSED SOURCE since 14 April 2026. The public repository is now Cal.diy under the MIT licence (changed from AGPL 3.0), with all enterprise code removed - there is no '/ee' licence any more. Removed: Teams, Organizations and role-based access, routing forms, the workflow automation engine, Insights, SAML/SSO, instant booking links, attributes, booking audit log, admin impersonation and the whole API v1. Kept: core scheduling, the app store, booking flows, API v2.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Pricing page, Terms, the repository README and LICENSE file, and two Cal.com blog posts (14 and 15 April 2026) read. Surprise: the usual description 'AGPLv3 with an /ee enterprise folder' is out of date. The hosted free plan is a single user, so team or round-robin scheduling across reps or interviewers is paid (12 USD per user/month). Self-hosted Cal.diy is F3 but single-user in practice (no teams, no workflows). Whether Cal.com itself can still be self-hosted under an enterprise contract is not stated on the pages read.

name: Formbricks (surveys)
free_limits: Hosted 'Hobby' plan: 0 USD forever, 1 workspace, 250 responses/month, link and in-product surveys, all question types and logic, full API access, hosted in Frankfurt. Pro: 74 USD/month billed yearly (89 USD monthly) - 3 workspaces, 2,000 responses/month, unlimited seats. Self-hosted Community Edition: free forever, no response cap stated, limited to one workspace.
commercial_use: Allowed - the licence page says 'You can use the software for free for personal and commercial use' and marks self-hosting for commercial purposes as included in the Community Edition.
auth_required: account (hosted); none for self-host
attribution_or_license_terms: Core is AGPLv3 (modified versions must be published under AGPLv3). Enterprise-licence-only when self-hosting: hiding 'Powered by Formbricks', white-label email follow-ups, teams and access roles, contact management and segments, quota management, workflows, unified feedback inbox, dashboards, audit logs, OIDC and SAML SSO, reCAPTCHA spam protection, two-factor authentication, more than one workspace. On the hosted Hobby plan, respondent identification, all integrations and custom webhooks, mobile SDKs and branding removal are Pro-only.
suggested_class: F3 free open source needing hosting
verification_note: Surveys pricing page (read in a browser), the Experience Suite pricing page and the self-hosting licence page read. Surprises: the hosted free tier is 250 responses/month (lower than the 1,000+ often quoted) and excludes integrations and custom webhooks; the main /pricing page now shows only the enterprise 'Experience Suite' with no published prices; two-factor authentication and SSO are enterprise-only even self-hosted. With about 230 users a single monthly pulse survey would nearly exhaust the hosted free tier, so self-hosting (F3) is the realistic free route; hosted Hobby is F2.

name: Jitsi Meet (meet.jit.si, JaaS, self-hosted)
free_limits: meet.jit.si: embedding in another web app is limited to 5-minute demo sessions (in effect since 18 May 2023); creating a room requires signing in with Google, GitHub or Facebook (since 24 August 2023); the Terms of Service limit no-cost use to an aggregate of 25 Active End Points per calendar month across all your accounts. JaaS: Developer plan free with 25 monthly active users; Basic 99 USD/month for 300; Standard 499 USD for 1,500; Business 999 USD for 3,000; overage 0.99 USD per MAU. Self-hosted: no limits other than your own server.
commercial_use: meet.jit.si: restricted - 'you should not place any reliance on the Service being offered for any commercial or other purposes'; 8x8 points business users to paid services. JaaS: allowed (commercial product). Self-hosted: allowed under Apache-2.0.
auth_required: meet.jit.si: account (Google/GitHub/Facebook) for the person who creates the room; JaaS: account plus JWT; self-hosted: none unless you configure it
attribution_or_license_terms: jitsi-meet is Apache License 2.0. meet.jit.si terms require leaving the Jitsi/8x8 branding visible when the service is integrated for third-party users.
suggested_class: F3 free open source needing hosting
verification_note: meet.jit.si Terms of Service, the Jitsi blog post on authentication (22 August 2023), the official forum announcement by a Jitsi team member (read in a browser), the 8x8 JaaS pricing page and the jitsi-meet LICENSE read. Surprise: embedding the public meet.jit.si in the platform is not a usable option (calls disconnect after 5 minutes), and the JaaS free tier of 25 monthly active users is far below 230 users. Only self-hosting (a server with a public IP and TURN) is free at this size; the alternative with no hosting is a plain link that opens meet.jit.si in a new tab, subject to the host sign-in and the 25-endpoint clause (terms dated October 2020; whether it is enforced was not confirmed). Whether guests can join without an account is not stated in the blog post.

name: FreeTSA.org RFC 3161 time-stamp authority
provider: FreeTSA (independent non-profit project, not a legal entity)
free_limits: Free. Usage policy: a maximum of one timestamping request per second per IP address; higher rates should use a dedicated instance. Endpoint https://freetsa.org/tsr (Content-Type: application/timestamp-query).
commercial_use: Not restricted by the usage policy; no commercial clause found.
auth_required: none
attribution_or_license_terms: None. Service is 'best-effort ... without any guarantee of availability, uptime, response times, or restoration times'; 'No Service Level Agreement (SLA) is offered'. Only the submitting IP address is recorded; hashes are not stored.
verification_note: Home page and usage-policy page read (the bare freetsa.org host refused the connection once; www.freetsa.org answered). Confirmed free with a 1 request/second/IP limit and no SLA. It is an independent hobby-scale project, not a company and not a qualified or accredited trust service, and the pages say nothing about legal validity - acceptable as supporting evidence of 'this file existed at this time', not as a legally recognised timestamp under Egyptian e-signature law. Plan for it being down: sign-off must never block on it.

name: Google Calendar API
free_limits: 'All standard use of the Google Calendar API is available at no additional cost.' Quotas: 1,000,000 requests per day per project (a billing threshold that cannot be increased), 10,000 requests per minute per project, 600 requests per minute per user per project.
commercial_use: Allowed - standard Google APIs terms; no commercial restriction on the quota page.
auth_required: OAuth (user consent) or a service account with domain-wide delegation on Workspace
attribution_or_license_terms: None beyond the Google APIs Terms of Service and the OAuth verification rules for sensitive Calendar scopes.
verification_note: Quota page, the create-events guide and the Events reference read. Surprises on the quota page: 'Exceeding the quota request limits is planned to incur charges to your Google Cloud billing account later in 2026' (details promised with at least 90 days' notice), and 'Cloud projects created on or after May 1, 2026 are subject to the new API quotas' (the new values are not listed on the page). Meet links: confirmed that an event gets a Google Meet conference by sending conferenceData.createRequest with a new requestId, conferenceSolutionKey type 'hangoutsMeet' and conferenceDataVersion=1 (status goes pending then success). NOT confirmed: the docs do not say whether this works for consumer (gmail.com) accounts versus Workspace accounts - they only say to check the calendar's conferenceProperties.allowedConferenceSolutionTypes; test it on the actual account before relying on it.

name: Google Maps Embed API
free_limits: 'Maps Embed usage is available at no charge.' 'There are no short-term (queries per second) or long-term (queries per day) limits on the Maps Embed API.' The pricing table lists the Embed SKU as Unlimited with no paid tier. Modes: place, view, directions, streetview, search - no per-mode charge is listed.
commercial_use: Allowed under the Google Maps Platform Terms of Service (a Cloud project with billing enabled is required to create the key).
auth_required: API key
attribution_or_license_terms: Google branding inside the iframe must not be altered. Key guidance: 'Google strongly recommends that you restrict your API keys' - apply an application restriction (websites) and an API restriction that leaves only Maps Embed API selected; an unrestricted key can call any Maps Platform service.
verification_note: Usage-and-billing page, the embedding guide, the get-api-key page and the Maps Platform pricing table read. Confirmed free and unlimited for all five modes on the current price list (the older split where directions, streetview and search were a paid 'Embed Advanced' SKU does not appear). The embed is display-only: nothing can be read back from it (no distances or coordinates).

name: Google Maps URLs (cross-platform deep links)
free_limits: No quota. 'You don't need a Google API key to use Maps URLs.' Formats: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=... and https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&origin=...&destination=... ; api=1 is required; each URL is limited to 2,048 characters.
commercial_use: Allowed - plain links that open Google Maps (app or web) on the user's device.
auth_required: none
attribution_or_license_terms: none
verification_note: Get-started page read: no API key needed. The page does not contain the words 'no charge'; the conclusion that it is free rests on the absence of a key and of any Maps URLs SKU in the pricing table (which was also read). The 2,048-character limit bounds how many waypoints one link can carry.

name: Google Maps Platform pricing (model in force since 1 March 2025)
free_limits: The 200 USD monthly credit is gone ('Free usage caps replace monthly $200 credit'). Free billable events per SKU per month: Essentials 10,000, Pro 5,000, Enterprise 1,000; caps reset on the 1st (Pacific time) and are aggregated across all projects on a billing account. SKU | category | free/month | USD per 1,000 after the cap (first paid band, up to 100,000): Dynamic Maps (Maps JavaScript map load) | Essentials | 10,000 | 7.00. Static Maps | Essentials | 10,000 | 2.00. Maps Embed | Essentials | Unlimited | free. Geocoding | Essentials | 10,000 | 5.00. Places Text Search Essentials (IDs Only) | Essentials | Unlimited | free. Places Text Search Pro | Pro | 5,000 | 32.00. Places Text Search Enterprise | Enterprise | 1,000 | 35.00. Places Nearby Search Pro | Pro | 5,000 | 32.00. Places Nearby Search Enterprise | Enterprise | 1,000 | 35.00. Place Details Essentials (IDs Only) | Essentials | Unlimited | free. Place Details Essentials | Essentials | 10,000 | 5.00. Place Details Pro | Pro | 5,000 | 17.00. Place Details Enterprise | Enterprise | 1,000 | 20.00. Autocomplete Requests | Essentials | 10,000 | 2.83. Autocomplete Session Usage | Essentials | Unlimited | free. Routes Compute Routes Essentials | 10,000 | 5.00; Pro | 5,000 | 10.00; Enterprise | 1,000 | 15.00. Routes Compute Route Matrix Essentials | 10,000 | 5.00; Pro | 5,000 | 10.00; Enterprise | 1,000 | 15.00 (Route Matrix is billed per element, origin x destination). Optional subscriptions: Starter 100 USD/month (50,000 combined calls), Essentials 275 USD (100,000), Pro 1,200 USD (250,000).
commercial_use: Allowed under the Google Maps Platform Terms; a billing account with a payment method is required, and usage above a cap is charged automatically unless quotas are capped in the Cloud console.
auth_required: API key (Cloud project with billing enabled)
attribution_or_license_terms: Service Specific Terms (last modified 28 October 2026): Google IDs may be cached - 'Customer may cache (a) place_id from Places API, Directions API, Geolocation API and Routes API'; the Places policies page says place IDs are exempt from the caching restrictions and may be stored indefinitely. Latitude/longitude from Places (14.3), Geocoding (6.3.1) and Routes (19.3) may be cached 'for up to 30 consecutive calendar days, after which Customer must delete' them. Geocoding 6.3.2 allows indefinite caching of lat/lng and address values only for the direct end-user-facing function, isolated to that one end user and not shared across users. Places, Geocoding and Routes content must not be used with a non-Google map (14.2, 6.2, 19.2). No pre-fetching, indexing or bulk storage of Google Maps content.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Billing overview, the pricing table, the Places policies page and the Service Specific Terms (clauses 6, 14, 19 and the Google ID caching clause) read. Confirmed the 10,000 / 5,000 / 1,000 model. Points that change a design: (1) there is no Essentials tier for Text Search or Nearby Search other than the free IDs-Only Text Search - any search that returns names or addresses is Pro at 32 USD per 1,000 after 5,000; (2) Google coordinates cannot be kept in the customer master beyond 30 days, only the place_id can; (3) Google results cannot be drawn on an OpenStreetMap/MapLibre map; (4) the field mask decides the SKU tier, so one extra field can move a call from Essentials to Enterprise. Prices are the first paid band in USD as rendered on the page today; verify in the Cloud billing console before committing.

name: Google Search JobPosting structured data and the Indexing API
free_limits: JobPosting markup has no fee or quota. Indexing API: 'All use of the Indexing API is available without payment'; default quotas 200 publish requests per day (URL_UPDATED and URL_DELETED together), 180 read-only getMetadata requests per minute, 380 requests per minute in total.
commercial_use: Allowed - intended for employers and job sites.
auth_required: none for the markup; a service account that is a verified owner of the site in Search Console for the Indexing API
attribution_or_license_terms: Required properties: datePosted, description, hiringOrganization, jobLocation, title (jobLocation may be replaced by applicantLocationRequirements for fully remote jobs). Policies: no expired postings (remove the page or set validThrough in the past), the page must offer a way to apply, and job details must be visible without logging in.
verification_note: JobPosting documentation, the Indexing API quota page and the Indexing API quickstart read. Confirmed: 'The Indexing API can only be used to crawl pages with either JobPosting or BroadcastEvent embedded in a VideoObject', and Google recommends it over sitemaps for job URLs. Submissions undergo spam detection and abuse can get access revoked. Conditions that matter here: each vacancy needs a PUBLIC page on the company's own domain that shows the full job and an apply route without a login, and whether Google's job experience is shown to searchers in Egypt was not checked.

name: Looker Studio - now named Data Studio (no-cost version)
free_limits: A no-cost version exists (Pro is described as 'all the features of the no-cost version of Data Studio, plus the enhanced enterprise capabilities'). PostgreSQL connector: maximum 150,000 rows per query (results beyond are truncated), queries may time out after three to five minutes, only tables in the public schema (others via a custom query), custom SQL must be a single statement, ASCII column headers only, no interval types. Documented PostgreSQL versions: 9.6, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14.
commercial_use: Allowed - no restriction on business use of the no-cost version found on the pages read.
auth_required: Google account; database host, port, user and password (or a JDBC URL), optionally TLS 1.2 with client certificate
attribution_or_license_terms: None. Data handling: Google's servers connect directly to the database, so it must accept connections from 142.251.74.0/23 (IPv6 2001:4860:4807::/48 optional) and the database credentials are entered into Google's service; with owner credentials every report viewer sees data through that one database login.
verification_note: PostgreSQL connector page and the Pro subscription overview read; the old cloud.google.com/looker-studio/pricing URL returns 404 and the product landing page would not render, so the Pro price was NOT confirmed. Surprises: Google's documentation now calls the product 'Data Studio' again (Looker Studio Pro is 'Data Studio Pro'); the connector's supported-version list stops at PostgreSQL 14, while Supabase runs newer major versions - connection may still work but is outside the documented list and was not tested; non-ASCII (Arabic) column headers are not supported. A reporting tool reading the production database directly means payroll and HR rows leave the application's access control - use a restricted read-only role and views, never the service role.

name: Google Postmaster Tools and Postmaster Tools API
free_limits: No price, plan or paid tier is documented anywhere on the pages read. Data appears only for a verified domain and may be missing 'if the total number of messages for a given day is too low' (no number given). API quotas are not published on the pages read.
commercial_use: Allowed - the tool is aimed at bulk senders.
auth_required: Google account plus domain verification (TXT or CNAME record in DNS) for the dashboard; OAuth 2.0 for the API (scopes postmaster, postmaster.domain, postmaster.traffic.readonly) with the API enabled in a Google Cloud project
attribution_or_license_terms: none
verification_note: API overview, API setup guide and the 'Set up Postmaster Tools' help article read. Confirmed: the API exists ('lets you gather statistics on bulk emails sent to Gmail users'), needs OAuth and a verified authentication domain (the DKIM d= domain or the SPF Return-Path domain). The pages opened never state a price in either direction - 'free' is supported only by the absence of any billing path and by a Google Workspace blog line seen as a search excerpt, not a page opened. Per the Gmail API release notes seen in search results, API v2 became generally available on 3 February 2026 and v1 is being retired - build against v2. With a sending volume of a few hundred mails a day to Gmail, the dashboards may simply stay empty.

name: openFDA API
free_limits: Without a key: 240 requests per minute and 1,000 requests per day per IP address. With a free API key: 240 requests per minute and 120,000 requests per day per key.
commercial_use: Allowed - 'You can copy, modify, distribute, and perform the work, even for commercial purposes, all without asking permission.' Exception: GMDN (device nomenclature) content needs a licence from The GMDN Agency for commercial services, mapping or AI training.
auth_required: none (optional free API key raises the daily limit)
attribution_or_license_terms: Public domain under CC0 1.0 unless marked otherwise. Attribution not required; FDA asks for the credit 'Data provided by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration' with a link to open.fda.gov. Provided 'as is', no warranty that data is error free; FDA may limit or stop the service.
verification_note: Authentication page and Terms of Service read; limits and CC0 confirmed. Relevance caveat, not a licensing one: openFDA covers products and adverse-event reports filed with the US FDA - it is not a source for Egyptian Drug Authority registrations or local brand names, so matches against an Egyptian product list will be by active ingredient at best.

name: DB-IP IP to City Lite / IP to Country Lite (alternative: MaxMind GeoLite2)
free_limits: DB-IP Lite: free download, CSV and MMDB, updated monthly, no account (a tick-box agreeing to the licence terms); City Lite has 7.78 million records versus 39.9 million in the paid database, accuracy index 77 versus 96. MaxMind GeoLite2: free with a MaxMind account and licence key; 30 database downloads per day; web service 1,000 lookups per day per service.
commercial_use: DB-IP Lite: allowed with attribution (CC BY 4.0). MaxMind GeoLite2: allowed 'for your own internal business purposes' under the GeoLite EULA, with restricted uses (see licence terms).
auth_required: DB-IP Lite: none. MaxMind GeoLite2: account plus licence key
attribution_or_license_terms: DB-IP Lite: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International; web applications 'must include a link back to DB-IP.com on pages that display or use results from the database', suggested IP Geolocation by DB-IP. MaxMind GeoLite2: GeoLite EULA (copyrightable elements CC BY-SA 4.0); credit 'This product includes GeoLite Data created by MaxMind, available from https://www.maxmind.com'; old database versions must be destroyed within 30 days of a new release; no disclosure to third parties without notifying MaxMind; may not be used as a factor in eligibility for credit, insurance, EMPLOYMENT purposes or government benefits, nor to identify a specific household, individual or street address.
verification_note: DB-IP Lite download page, MaxMind's GeoLite developer page and the GeoLite EULA read. DB-IP: CC BY 4.0, monthly, link-back required wherever results are shown (an internal audit screen counts). Surprise on the alternative: the GeoLite EULA bars use 'for employment purposes' and for locating a specific individual - a poor fit for an HR platform that would attach IP location to an employee's login or attendance, and it adds a 30-day forced-update duty; DB-IP Lite has neither restriction on the page read. City-level IP location in Egypt is coarse on any free database (mobile carriers route through a few cities) - usable for country or suspicious-login hints, not for proving where a rep was.

name: Telegram Bot API
free_limits: No fee for normal use. Documented limits: avoid more than one message per second in a single chat (short bursts tolerated, then HTTP 429); in a group, not more than 20 messages per minute; bulk notifications not more than about 30 messages per second overall. Optional Paid Broadcasts raise this to up to 1,000 messages per second at 0.1 Telegram Stars per message above the free 30 per second.
commercial_use: Allowed - no commercial restriction in the Bot API documentation or FAQ.
auth_required: API key (bot token from @BotFather)
attribution_or_license_terms: None. Telegram Bot Platform developer terms apply.
verification_note: Bot FAQ and the Bot API reference read (current version shown: Bot API 10.4, 9 November 2026). Confirmed present in the reference: sendPoll ('Use this method to send a native poll'), InlineKeyboardMarkup, CallbackQuery and answerCallbackQuery. The FAQ words the price as bots being able to message users 'at no cost' by default rather than a blanket 'the API is free' sentence. The two pages disagree on the Stars balance needed to switch on Paid Broadcasts (FAQ: 100,000 Stars and 100,000 monthly users; API page: 10,000 Stars) - irrelevant at 230 users. A bot can only message a user who has started it first.

name: WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API) pricing
free_limits: Per-message pricing since 1 July 2025; Meta charges only for messages from the business to users. SINCE 1 OCTOBER 2026: service (non-template, 24-hour-window) messages are charged, with a free tier of 1,000 delivered service messages per business phone number per month (no roll-over); utility templates sent inside an open customer service window are charged at the utility rate (they were free from 1 July 2025 to 30 September 2026). Still free: messages inside a free entry point window opened from a click-to-WhatsApp ad or Page button. Egypt is its own market on the rate card; USD rates shown by Meta's rate selector today: marketing 0.0644, utility 0.0036, authentication 0.0036, service 0.0036, authentication-international 0.0650 per delivered message. Service messages have no volume tiers; utility and authentication do.
commercial_use: Allowed - a commercial product; a payment method on file is required (Meta stopped delivering service messages from 1 October 2026 for accounts without one).
auth_required: account (Meta Business portfolio, WhatsApp Business Account, system-user access token; business verification for higher limits and for Flows)
attribution_or_license_terms: WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy and Meta terms; users must opt in; templates need category approval.
verification_note: Meta developer pricing page, its 'updates to pricing' page, the 'upcoming pricing updates for service and utility messages' page, and the whatsappbusiness.com pricing page with its rate selector (read in a browser for Egypt/USD) were read. BIG SURPRISE: the widely held 'service replies are free and utility templates are free inside the 24-hour window' stopped being true on 1 October 2026 - only the first 1,000 service messages per number per month are free now. Meta's own marketing page still says 'we do not charge for service messages, or for utility messages businesses send in response to users', which contradicts the developer documentation; the developer documentation is the billing authority and the rate selector already shows a service rate for Egypt. Free-entry-point window length: developer page says 'up to 7 days', marketing page says 72 hours - unresolved. NOT confirmed: any statement that WhatsApp Flows is free - the Flows pages read say nothing on cost; a Flow is sent inside a template or interactive message and would be billed by that message's category (inference). Rates are what the selector displayed today; the downloadable rate card file was not opened.

name: Egyptian Tax Authority e-Invoicing SDK / API
free_limits: No fee or free-of-charge statement appears on any SDK page read. Rate limits per registered ERP system: Get Recent Documents 3 requests/second; Get Document, Get Document Details and Search Documents 2 requests/second; Get Document Printout (PDF) 1 request per 5 seconds; HTTP 429 with Retry-After when exceeded. Access token lifetime 1 hour.
commercial_use: Intended for registered taxpayers' ERP and POS systems; not a general public API.
auth_required: OAuth client credentials - a Client ID and Client Secret issued for an ERP system registered in the taxpayer's ETA profile (Basic auth to the identity service, grant_type=client_credentials); submitting documents additionally needs an eSeal X.509 signing certificate
attribution_or_license_terms: None stated. Environments: pre-production (api.preprod.invoicing.eta.gov.eg, id.preprod.eta.gov.eg) and production (api.invoicing.eta.gov.eg, id.eta.gov.eg).
verification_note: NOT VERIFIED AS FREE: the SDK home, getting-started, FAQ, API governance, login and Get Document pages were read and none mentions cost in either direction; the eSeal certificate is bought from a licensed provider (not confirmed on these pages). What IS confirmed: there is an API to fetch a document by UUID - GET /api/v1.0/documents/{uuid}/raw (source XML/JSON with ETA metadata), plus Get Document Details (with validation results) and Get Document Printout (PDF). Access is limited to the parties: the issuer sees any status; the receiver sees only Valid, Rejected or Cancelled documents issued to them; a profile tagged 'B2B Deny ERP Document Retrieval' gets 403. So it can verify invoices the company issued or received, not arbitrary third-party invoices. The SDK home page shows a last-updated date of 08-12-2022.

name: OneSignal (push, in-app, email) - Free plan
free_limits: Free plan (0 USD/month): web push with a maximum of 10,000 subscribers per send; 'Unlimited Mobile Push Notifications' but only 'for organizations with up to 1,000 monthly active users'; in-app messaging and Live Activities under the same 1,000-MAU condition; email 10,000 sends/month; 3 active journeys, 6 segments, 6 data tags; reporting history up to 30 days. Not included: message events and their retention, throttling, frequency capping, intelligent delivery, time-delayed sends, confirmed receipt, advanced analytics, CSV exports, notification history API, premium integrations, SLA, prioritised support. Growth plan starts at 19 USD/month (0.012 USD per mobile MAU, 0.004 USD per web push subscriber).
commercial_use: Allowed - the free plan is offered 'for individuals and organizations just starting out'; no non-commercial clause found.
auth_required: account (App ID and REST API key)
attribution_or_license_terms: Terms: 'Licensee grants OneSignal a worldwide license to access and use SDK data for the purpose of providing the Service' and OneSignal may 'make data available to third parties as necessary'. 'The Company may terminate your subscription to the Free Services due to your inactivity', for exceeding storage or compute limits, or for using a premium integration without a paid plan; either party may terminate without notice.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Pricing page (read by fetch and in a browser) and the Terms of Use read. Surprise: free mobile push is no longer 'unlimited subscribers' - it is conditioned on up to 1,000 monthly active users, which 230 users fit inside. No clause specific to free accounts about selling data was found in the terms read (the older belief that free-plan data is monetised was not confirmed and not disproved - the privacy policy was not read). Web push on iPhone requires the site to be installed to the home screen; employee device identifiers would sit with a US processor.

name: Resend pricing
free_limits: Free: 3,000 emails/month, daily limit 100 emails/day, 3 custom domains, 1 webhook endpoint, 30-day data retention (as read on the page). Pro: 20 USD/month for 50,000 emails (35 USD for 100,000), no daily limit, 10 domains, overage 0.90 USD per 1,000 if pay-as-you-go is enabled. Extra domains add-on 20 USD/month; dedicated IP 30 USD/month.
commercial_use: Allowed.
auth_required: API key (account, verified sending domain)
attribution_or_license_terms: None. Inbound: receiving exists on every plan including Free; 'Each received email counts towards your transactional emails quota'. Inboxes are billed at 1 USD per month each and share the same quota.
verification_note: Pricing page and its FAQ read (fetch plus a direct read of the comparison table). Confirmed 3,000/month and 100/day on Free, Pro at 20 USD, inbound on all plans and counted against the sending quota. Two figures differ from what is usually quoted and come from the comparison table as rendered today: 3 custom domains on Free (commonly remembered as 1) and 30-day retention on Free - re-read in the dashboard before designing around either. The 100/day cap is the binding one for a 230-person platform: one broadcast to all staff exceeds it.

name: Brevo (formerly Sendinblue) - Free plan
free_limits: 300 emails/day once the account is approved for sending (the daily limit resets each day and does not roll over). The Free plan 'is limited to one (1) User only' and carries contact, automation and sending limits. Per Brevo's help-centre FAQ (seen as a search excerpt; the article itself returned 403), transactional emails beyond the daily limit are held in a retry queue of up to 1,000 and anything beyond that is not delivered.
commercial_use: Allowed - no non-commercial clause; liability on the Free plan is limited to the SLA remedies.
auth_required: API key or SMTP credentials (account; sending requires account approval)
attribution_or_license_terms: Terms 3.4, user account inactivity: 'We may terminate your account if You have not logged in the Software or not performed one action or command in the Software for a period of six (6) months or more' - an email notice is sent first, then the account and its content are permanently deleted with no restoration.
suggested_class: F2 permanent free tier with limits
verification_note: Pricing page (its embedded FAQ and plan data) and the Terms of Service read; the help-centre limits article could not be opened. Confirmed 300 emails/day, one user and the six-month inactivity termination clause. NOT confirmed: the words 'free forever' (the pricing page says an account automatically starts on a Free plan with no end date mentioned), the current contact cap, and whether Brevo branding is forced on free transactional emails. If Brevo were kept only as a dormant fallback sender, the inactivity clause means it can be deleted after six months without a login or action - whether API sends alone count as activity is not stated.
